title: Friends: Treating Social Networks Like Side Projects
author: Brian Cullinan
summary: Philosophizing on friendship dynamics: treating relationships like engineering projects and surrounding yourself with vocal critics who won't hesitate to point out your bugs.
content_html:
Friends: Treating Social Networks Like Side Projects

Published on April 23, 2008 by Brian Cullinan

Managing real-world peer networks: surrounding yourself with people who aren't afraid to call out your flawed logic.

Disclaimer: This isn't LiveJournal, so I'll keep the emo-rambling to a minimum. But managing your personal network is essentially a long-term engineering project.

The Peer Review Process

Forget generic motivational quotes—we are the product of aspirations inspired by our friends. The best friends aren't the ones who validate every foolish idea you have; they are the harsh code reviewers of your life. They offer blunt criticism, call out bad logic, and force you to hold yourself to a higher standard.

If your inner circle isn't articulate, intelligent, and ready to stand up for their principles, it's time to refactor your social graph.
modern_insight_2026: A 21-year-old undergrad writing 'managing your relationships is a project' is peak CS major behavior. Treating friendships like peer code reviews and bug reports was just an early sign of an engineer who approaches every human interaction like a system optimization problem.

title: Relationship Advice for the Young Hearted: Quoting Scrubs, Johnny Cash & Shakespeare
author: Brian Cullinan
summary: An epic manifesto on surviving college relationships: managing crazy in small doses, avoiding grass-is-greener lust traps, and scheduling date nights like production cron jobs.
content_html:
Relationship Advice for the Young Hearted: Quoting Scrubs, Johnny Cash & Shakespeare

Published on April 20, 2008 by Brian Cullinan

Scheduling date nights: bringing structural predictability and execution discipline to romantic partnerships.

After navigating a few relationship landmines, I felt compelled to drop some unsolicited relationship wisdom on my readers. Take it or throw it in the trash.

Rule 1: Dole Out the Crazy in Small Pieces

As Carla wisely told the Janitor on Scrubs: "You have to dole out your crazy in little pieces, you can't do it all at once." Dump your full list of weird hobbies and quirks on someone during week one, and they will run for the hills.

Rule 2: The Grass Is Greener Delusion

Breaking off an existing relationship just because you caught feelings for someone new is almost always a trap. Lust blinds you to red flags (as Shakespeare pointed out). In most cases, once you actually get to know the 'shiny new person,' you realize they have just as many bugs as anyone else.

Rule 3: Schedule Date Nights Like System Maintenance

To keep the fire burning (cue Johnny Cash's Ring of Fire), you have to balance work, school, and social circles. Lock down a recurring Date Night calendar block to keep the core thread alive without burning out.
modern_insight_2026: Quoting Carla from Scrubs, Johnny Cash, and Shakespeare in a single college blog post to explain relationship dynamics is hilarious. But recommending structured date nights and active communication actually held up pretty well over time.
